summary: Independent primary-source review strengthens two distinct 2036 constraint hypotheses without changing canonical state. First, large-load/data-center growth is not only a generation-equipment problem: FERC's June 18, 2026 orders across all six RTO/ISOs show interconnection rules, transmission service, generation adequacy and electrically-proximate generation can themselves govern speed-to-power. Second, purpose-built AV deployment faces a regulatory/certification throughput constraint separate from autonomy software: NHTSA is simultaneously modernizing FMVSS/exemption pathways and auditing Tesla Cybercab self-certification after commercial deployment. These are constraint-migration signals, not company scores.

materialFindings.finding: Large-load interconnection is a distinct successor bottleneck: FERC ordered all six jurisdictional regional grid operators to justify or reform tariffs for data centers and other large loads, including flexible transmission service and study of electrically proximate generation, with generation-adequacy reporting required.

Counterfactual/falsifier for the grid constraint: if regional reforms materially compress interconnection timelines without requiring substantial network upgrades or new generation, regulatory/interconnection throughput should lose causal weight relative to equipment capacity. FERC explicitly identifies flexible load and bring-your-own-new-generation structures as mechanisms that can reduce upgrade needs.

Purpose-built AV certification/regulatory throughput is independently evidenced as distinct from technical autonomy capability: NHTSA opened a September 4, 2026 audit of Tesla Cybercab self-certification after commercial deployment while its AV Framework is modernizing FMVSS and using temporary exemptions for nontraditional vehicle designs.

AV constraint falsifier: if purpose-built AV developers can repeatedly obtain/maintain compliant certification or exemptions at commercial scale without material deployment delay, certification throughput should be downgraded from bottleneck to ordinary compliance cost. NHTSA's Zoox exemption pathway provides a live alternative route and therefore prevents treating certification as an absolute barrier.

proposedCanonicalChanges.proposal: Chief may consider a sourced causal node/edge for large-load interconnection/regulatory throughput as a successor constraint to generation/grid equipment, with 2026-2030 horizon and the stated timeline-compression falsifier.

Chief may consider purpose-built AV certification/regulatory throughput as a non-duplicative autonomy deployment constraint, with 2026-2030 horizon and repeated scalable certification/exemption success as falsifier.

unknowns: Entity-level economic sensitivity of individual AV companies to certification delay is not yet normalized.
Magnitude and duration of interconnection reform effects by RTO/ISO remain unknown until tariff responses and realized queue outcomes are observable.

peerRequests.request: When underwriting AV-exposed companies, separate technical autonomy readiness from certification/exemption readiness and quantify deployment dependence where primary disclosures allow.
Track realized large-load interconnection timelines and tariff outcomes rather than assuming FERC reform immediately removes speed-to-power constraints.
